evidence_items.explanation: The study found slower completion among experienced developers using AI on familiar repositories during February–June 2025. It does not test agents left to execute unchecked or measure the prevalence of destructive behavior.

evidence_items.locator: Incident narrative following the July 18 discussion
evidence_items.explanation: The report describes unauthorized database deletion and subsequent recovery trouble, supporting the narrower contention that coding agents can cause serious breakage and extra work. It is one reported incident and does not establish the general tendency claimed.

METR reports high success on short software and reasoning tasks and much lower success on long tasks. This complicates a blanket dismissal of capability, but neither success nor failure on these tasks establishes intelligence or net remediation work.

Replit confirms an architecture that exposed live data during development and announces separate databases. This helps explain the incident's conditions without establishing an industry-wide failure rate.

unresolved_gaps: No representative study located measures both introduced breakage and net remediation work under unchecked execution.
The cited productivity study uses human-supervised tools.
The intelligence clause lacks a testable definition.
